Legs.Subject: UnitFraction16.op_Multiply — its own uint truncate-and-correct at the 2⁻¹⁶ grid, ties to even
Legs.Against: Oracles.UnitFractionProduct → Oracles.RoundDyadic at shift 16 over BigInteger, no Puck.Maths call. ENVELOPE: the shared operand fold Subjects.UnitFraction16Raw is the low sixteen bits of the draw — TOTAL and unbiased, unlike the closed interval's saturating fold — but it sends the committed edge set onto only six distinct raws {0, 1, 256, 32768, 65280, 65535}, so the edge square is a corner battery and the breadth comes from the edge-biased random stream and the stratified frontier. The tie IS reached inside that corner: 32768 × 65535 rounds a half up off an odd truncation and 32768 × 1 rounds one down off an even one

Legs.Subject: the product cannot leave the half-open interval: the largest pair rounds to 2¹⁶ − 2, so the type is closed under multiplication with no saturation anywhere — the fact the closed interval spends its thirty-third bit to obtain and this type gets for free
UnitFraction16.op_Division — the truncate-and-correct on the sixteen-bit-shifted dividend, saturating at MaxValue
Legs.Against: Oracles.UnitFractionQuotient — the exact ratio (x·2¹⁶)/y divided in BigInteger, one ties-to-even rounding, then a clamp at 2¹⁶ − 1; the oracle divides in arbitrary width and shares no code and no rounding substrate with the subject. ENVELOPE: the tie 2·(x·2¹⁶ mod y) == y is unreachable at EVERY legal operand pair — the dividend carries sixteen factors of two and every divisor below 2¹⁶ carries at most fifteen — so the correction's equal-to-half branch is dead on both sides and agreement pins the truncation, the round-up and the saturation only

Legs.Subject: the ordered operand fold Subjects.UnitFraction16Ratio divides the SMALLER sampled raw by the LARGER, so the sweep lives in the sub-one regime where the rounding actually fires; the saturating corner is still reached on the edge square's diagonal, where equal raws divide to exactly one, and it is pinned outright by the quotient ladder in unit-fraction16.construction-and-refusals

Legs.Subject: the primary constructor and FromRawBits are one fact — both preserve the raw and produce equal values at every swept raw

the constants have the structure they claim: Zero, MinValue, AdditiveIdentity and default coincide and are neutral for both sums; a value is its own additive inverse and its own exclusive-or annihilator; both complements are involutions; Epsilon adds exactly one raw; MinValue is neutral for Max and MaxValue for Min; and the saturating pair stops exactly at MaxValue and at zero

the De Morgan pair holds between the bitwise complement and the two order selections: complement(max) == min(complements) and complement(min) == max(complements), pinned at the carrier so a material built on it inherits the fact — the same statement closed-unit.bounded-ops-exact makes for the interval's ARITHMETIC complement, here for the bitwise one
UnitFraction16.op_LeftShift and op_RightShift over a sampled amount and the committed ladder {0, 1, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, −1}
Legs.Against: (raw · 2^(s & 31)) mod 2¹⁶ and raw >> (s & 31) in BigInteger, inline in Subjects.UnitFraction16ShiftsMatchOracle. The mask is re-derived from the LANGUAGE rule — the operand promotes to a thirty-two-bit word, so a C# shift count acts modulo thirty-two — and not from the kernel, which never spells it

Legs.Subject: op_UnsignedRightShift equals op_RightShift at every swept raw and amount, which is what the unsigned storage makes it and what the member documents

the amounts at and beyond the mask are part of the statement, not an accident: an amount of thirty-two is the IDENTITY and a negative amount shifts by its masked residue, which is the modulo-thirty-two promotion rule all three shift members now document — mask 31, not 15

the declared grid is one fact: FractionBitCount == TotalBitCount == 16, MaxValue.Value == 2¹⁶ − 1, Epsilon.Value == 1, and Zero, MinValue, AdditiveIdentity and default(UnitFraction16) all coincide at raw zero
the half-open contract itself: MaxValue + Epsilon WRAPS to zero while AddSaturating stops at MaxValue — the type has no one, which is exactly what separates it from UnitInterval32

the thirteen-raw construction ladder — zero and its neighbourhood, the byte seam, the exact half either side, and the top either side — is preserved bit-for-bit by both construction routes, the primary constructor and FromRawBits

Legs.Subject: the refusal contract: every refused spelling leaves the default value behind on both TryParse routes and makes both Parse routes throw FormatException. The ladder includes the two SIGN spellings and the exponent spelling, which the type's style flags refuse outright — so the whole negative branch of the shared parsing helper, including its maximumNegativeMagnitudeRaw parameter, is unreachable for this type

out-of-range text is REFUSED, never clamped: '0.99998474121093751' exceeds MaxValue by one unit of the seventeenth decimal place and is refused even though rounding would carry it back onto MaxValue, while '0.99998474121093749' is accepted and rounds up onto it. The parser tests the exact value before rounding, which makes the post-rounding overflow check unreachable — ENVELOPE
the null-string contract: TryParse(null) returns false leaving the default, and Parse(null) throws ArgumentNullException naming the 's' parameter
